meta.name: MusicLinkd Design Tokens
meta.note:
v9.0 (2026-08-29) is a DELETION pass plus dual authoring, not an expansion. v8 documented a system whose live CSS had grown to 248 custom properties in one :root — 26 radius tokens, 29 spacing, 21 duration, 20 opacity, 14 type, 11 shadow — where every token past the 4-step core was a provable exact duplicate (--r-sm = 8px = --radius-1; --op-hover = 0.08 = --opacity-1; --el-1 = --shadow-1). Those aliases carried zero information and made the contrast between steps unreadable, which is the entire point of a 4-step exponential scale. v9 keeps ONE name per value. No scale may exceed 4 steps.

The second change is dual authoring: every token that differs between web and native now carries explicit $web / $android / $ios forms. This closes the real native gap — clamp() does not exist on Android or iOS, and native motion is spring physics rather than duration+bezier, so a single web-shaped value could never have been handed to a Compose engineer.

Also repaired here: 155 var() references in styleguide.html pointed at names that were never defined anywhere in the file (--white ×62 with no fallback, --surface-subtle ×26, --r-avatar ×14, --ease ×12, --text-2 ×7, --navy ×4, --ink ×3). Verified resolving to empty string on the deployed page, 2026-08-29. The names that represent real values (--white, --surface-subtle, --ink) are defined properly below; the rest were duplicates of existing tokens and are retired.

palette.$description: Governing visual rule, set by the brand owner 2026-08-29 against Apple Music / Shazam / SoundCloud / Instagram / Tinder: THE CHROME IS MONOCHROME, THE MEDIA CARRIES ALL THE COLOUR. Black, grey and white build every surface and control. Album art, studio photography, waveforms and profile imagery supply all saturation. Pink is a ~10-15% accent — state, selection, focus, brand mark — and is never a surface fill. Approximate budget: black ~60%, grey+white ~30%, pink ~10-15%.

removed.purple: #8B5CF6 and --purple-container #F3E8FF were live in styleguide.html's :root despite frontend/guide/README.md's Boundaries section explicitly forbidding purple brand tokens. Deleted.
removed.navy: #0D0B26 removed per the black/grey/white + pink palette rule. It was referenced by semantic.surface.navyHero and by webapp's theme-color meta tag; both move to foundation.color.ink.

darkMode.$description: Deliberately not built. The system is light-only and monochrome — that is a position, not a gap. v8's semantic.action.dark block is removed rather than left dangling. Revisit only on explicit instruction; when it happens the decision that must be made first is the dark elevation rule (Gestalt drops shadows for a 1px border, Material raises surface tint) — MusicLinkd has never made that call.

tokenBudget.$description: Enforced by scripts/build-tokens.mjs, which fails the build if the generated CSS exceeds the ceiling. Measured live on /guide/styleguide 2026-08-29 before this pass.

gestaltSource.$description: Gestalt is REFERENCE ONLY, per frontend/guide/README.md — never a runtime dependency. v8 inlined its full scales into this file (17 spacing steps, 12 rounding, 11 duration); those are removed because they were being consumed as if they were MusicLinkd tokens. What survives from Gestalt is the 423 Apache-2.0 icons already extracted to musiclinkd-system/icons/.

color.$description: 12 colours. Neutrals do the work; pink accents; three status colours. Any saturation beyond this comes from media, never from chrome.

ink.$description: Primary action AND primary text. The single darkest value — replaces --black, --text and the retired --navy.

white.$description: Card and sheet fill. Was referenced 62 times in styleguide.html and never defined — the single worst broken token in the system.

surface.$description: Subtle raised/sunken fill — search bars, inactive segments, skeletons. Absorbs both v8's --surface-alt (#F8F8FB) and --surface-2 (#F1F5F9), which were visually indistinguishable, and the 26 broken --surface-subtle references.

muted.$description: Secondary text, metadata, placeholder. Absorbs the 7 broken --text-2 references. Darkened from styleguide.html's #7D7D8E on 2026-08-29: that value measured 3.94:1 on --color-paper, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 floor for normal text, and it is the colour of EVERY piece of secondary copy in the app — so the whole app failed AA. #6E6E7D measures 4.89 on paper, 5.01 on white and 4.73 on surface.

pink.$description: Brand accent — focus ring, selection, active tab, brand mark, waveform progress. NEVER a surface fill and never the primary CTA.

pinkPressed.$description: Two jobs, one token. (1) Pressed/active state of an accent control. (2) The ONLY pink permitted for TEXT: the brand pink #EA4C89 measures 3.48:1 on paper and fails AA as text, while this measures 5.24. Rule: pink FILLS and marks use --color-pink; pink TEXT uses --color-pink-pressed. Darkened from #D93C77 (4.21, still failing) on 2026-08-29.

pinkContainer.$description: The one permitted tinted surface — accent chips, progress tracks. Used sparingly.

inkPressed.$description: Pressed state of a primary (black) control — lifts off pure black so the press is visible

space.$description: 4-step exponential (r=2). Identical on web (px) and native (dp).

3.$description: Card padding, default gap, screen gutter

1.$description: Chips, small controls, inline media thumbs

4.$description: Pill / full round — buttons, chips, avatars. Functional, not a scale step. Absorbs the 14 broken --r-avatar references: an avatar is radius-4.

size.$description: Control heights. Doubles as the touch-target scale — 3 IS the 48dp accessibility minimum and 4 IS the 56dp comfortable target, so no separate touch tokens are needed (v8 had both, duplicated).

1.$description: Chip, small button, compact icon button

3.$description: MINIMUM TOUCH TARGET. Android 48dp (Material), iOS 44pt (HIG). Primary buttons, list rows, tab bar items.

4.$description: Comfortable target — primary CTAs, FAB, player controls

type.$description: 4 steps. Web uses fluid clamp() between a 360px and 1440px viewport. NATIVE CANNOT — clamp() does not exist on Android or iOS — so each step carries an explicit sp ramp (Android) and a Dynamic Type style (iOS), both of which scale with the user's OS font-size setting. RULE: every step's web clamp MINIMUM equals its Android sp value (12/16/22/32). The preview is approved at phone width, so if the web minimum sat below the sp value the preview would be showing smaller text than the app will ever render — which is what happened before 2026-08-29 (web 10/14/20/28 against native 12/16/22/32; the caption measured 10.03px on screen). The clamp still scales UP toward the max on wider viewports, where there is no native counterpart to disagree with. Families: Inter Tight for display/titles, Inter for body/labels.

1.$description: Micro labels, captions, badges, metadata, timestamps

2.$description: Body copy, default UI text, list item titles

3.$description: Section headings, card titles, screen titles

4.$description: Display — hero headlines, now-playing track title, the one big number on a screen

font.$description: Tokenized for the first time — v8 left these as hardcoded strings, and webapp/index.html already referenced an undefined var(--font-body). --font-mono is retired: it named 'JetBrains Mono', which was never loaded by any @font-face or Google Fonts link, so every use silently fell back to the generic monospace.

elevation.$description: Reduced from 4 shadows (plus two parallel duplicate scales, --el-* and --gestalt-elevation-*) to 2. The reference apps — Apple Music, Instagram — separate surfaces with hairline borders and background contrast, not stacked shadows. Two levels is what a flat monochrome system actually uses: one resting lift, one floating overlay. Android maps to Compose elevation dp; iOS to a shadow modifier.

1.$description: Resting — cards that need to lift off the canvas at all. Prefer a --color-line border first.

2.$description: Floating — bottom sheet, FAB, menu, mini-player, modal

motion.$description: Dual-authored. Web gets duration + cubic-bezier; native gets spring physics, which is what Compose and SwiftUI actually animate with — a duration is not translatable to a spring and pretending otherwise was the core web-shaped assumption in v8. Four steps, matched pairwise.

1.$description: Press, ripple, toggle, chip select — must feel instant

2.$description: Icon change, colour change, hover lift, dismissal

3.$description: Sheet reveal, card lift, shared-element / container transform

$android.note: Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy — the one step allowed to overshoot

4.$description: Entrance, modal, splash, expressive moments (the Shazam result reveal)

zIndex.$description: Web-only — native uses composition order, not a z scale. 4 tiers, exponential. Elements needing strict order inside one tier use a calc() offset off that tier rather than a 5th token.

1.$description: Persistent chrome — top bar, bottom tab bar

3.$description: Transient overlays — sheet, modal, and their scrims

interaction.$description: Gesture thresholds. v8 recorded these as '$description: No MusicLinkd token — hardcoded in App.tsx'. The real values already existed in styleguide.html's --int-app-* block and had simply never been lifted into the source of truth. Doing that here is what lets SwipeDeckBlock and the bottom sheet stop hardcoding them, and gives Compose a number to match.

swipeThreshold.$description: Distance past which a swipe commits — sheet dismiss, swipe deck, row actions

dragThreshold.$description: Movement before a drag is recognised over a tap

semantic.$description: ROLE DOCUMENTATION ONLY — deliberately emits no CSS custom properties. Every entry below whose value is a 1:1 alias of a foundation colour (action.primary = color.ink, surface.canvas = color.paper, text.primary = color.ink) would be a second name for the same value, which is precisely how v8 reached 248 tokens. On web, use the foundation token directly: --color-ink IS the primary action and the primary text. This block survives because the Compose and SwiftUI exports DO want role names (MLColor.actionPrimary), and because it records which foundation colour fills which role. media.* and haptic.* below are not aliases and do emit.

primary.$description: The CTA colour is BLACK, not pink (corrected 2026-08-16 by the brand owner and re-confirmed 2026-08-29)

accent.$description: Focus, selection, active state, brand mark — never a CTA fill

onMedia.$description: Text over artwork — always paired with the scrim gradient below, never placed on raw imagery

media.$description: The palette rule made operational. Media is the only element permitted to carry saturation, so it needs its own scrim and aspect contract to stay legible.

scrim.$description: Applied under any text laid over artwork

haptic.$description: v8 had three entries naming Android constants only, which is unusable for an iOS build and unusable on web. Each entry now maps all three platforms. Web uses the Vibration API and degrades silently where unsupported (iOS Safari has no Vibration API at all — that is expected, not a bug).

selection.$description: Chip select, tab change, waveform scrub detent

platform.$description: Where web and native genuinely differ. v8 recorded platform.app as 'consumesTokensFrom: Nothing yet' — these values now have real consumers in frontend/guide/system/ and are emitted into the Compose export.

safeArea.$description: Edge-to-edge is enforced for apps targeting current Android SDK levels and is the default on iOS, so insets are mandatory rather than optional. Web reads env(); native reads WindowInsets (Compose) / safeAreaInsets (SwiftUI). The px numbers are fallbacks only, for browsers with no env() support.

windowSize.$description: Replaces v8's px breakpoints, which disagreed with themselves — styleguide.html declared 768/1024/1440 while the Gestalt block declared 576/768/1312, and neither is a size class. These are Material 3 WindowSizeClass widths, which is what Compose actually branches on and what foldables and tablets report.

medium.$description: ≥600dp — large phone landscape, small tablet, unfolded inner display
